{
  "summary": "Hardens external signer PSBT handling in the wallet by merging the returned PSBT into the original instead of replacing it wholesale, verifying matching PSBT versions, rejecting finalized inputs, and rejecting signatures that declare or use unsafe sighash flags (SIGHASH_NONE or SIGHASH_SINGLE). It also revamps the functional test mock signer to use a dedicated offline descriptor wallet capable of generating valid and maliciously tampered signatures across various descriptor types, and enforces IWYU for `src/external_signer.cpp`.",
  "problem": "Bitcoin Core previously replaced its outgoing PSBT with whatever PSBT the external signer returned, trusting external hardware devices or bridge utilities not to alter outputs, amounts, or scripts. A buggy or compromised signer could return signatures over altered outputs, use sighash types that allow third parties to mutate transactions post-signing, or finalize inputs to conceal sighash types. Testing these scenarios was previously infeasible because the functional test mock signer could only replay static, pre-recorded PSBTs.",
  "evidence": [
    "PR description: 'Previously the PSBT returned by the external signer replaced the original wholesale, trusting the signer not to modify the transaction. Merge it instead. This rejects a response that describes a different transaction.'",
    "Commit 5c7a917300: 'A signature with SIGHASH_NONE or SIGHASH_SINGLE doesn't commit to all outputs, letting anyone alter them after signing. Reject a PSBT from an external signer that declares such a sighash type or contains signatures made with one.'",
    "PR description notes it absorbs test scenarios from closed PR #35358."

This PR hardens external signer processing by merging signer responses into the original PSBT, verifying matching PSBT versions, rejecting finalized inputs, and disallowing unsafe sighash types like SIGHASH_NONE or SIGHASH_SINGLE. It also revamps the functional test mock signer to run an offline descriptor wallet that can simulate misbehaving or stripped signer responses, and enforces IWYU for the external signer module.",

result.summary: Hardens external signer PSBT handling in the wallet by merging the returned PSBT into the original instead of replacing it wholesale, verifying matching PSBT versions, rejecting finalized inputs, and rejecting signatures that declare or use unsafe sighash flags (SIGHASH_NONE or SIGHASH_SINGLE). It also revamps the functional test mock signer to use a dedicated offline descriptor wallet capable of generating valid and maliciously tampered signatures across various descriptor types, and enforces IWYU for `src/external_signer.cpp`.
result.problem: Bitcoin Core previously replaced its outgoing PSBT with whatever PSBT the external signer returned, trusting external hardware devices or bridge utilities not to alter outputs, amounts, or scripts. A buggy or compromised signer could return signatures over altered outputs, use sighash types that allow third parties to mutate transactions post-signing, or finalize inputs to conceal sighash types. Testing these scenarios was previously infeasible because the functional test mock signer could only replay static, pre-recorded PSBTs.
evidence: PR description: 'Previously the PSBT returned by the external signer replaced the original wholesale, trusting the signer not to modify the transaction. Merge it instead. This rejects a response that describes a different transaction.'

Commit 5c7a917300: 'A signature with SIGHASH_NONE or SIGHASH_SINGLE doesn't commit to all outputs, letting anyone alter them after signing. Reject a PSBT from an external signer that declares such a sighash type or contains signatures made with one.'
PR description notes it absorbs test scenarios from closed PR #35358.
result.changed_since_previous: No substantive architectural changes; commit restructuring and test refactors (such as reusing `create_outpoints` in `wallet_signer.py` and adding co-authors).
result.card: Bitcoin Core previously trusted external signers completely, replacing the wallet's PSBT wholesale with whatever data the signer returned. This PR hardens external signer processing by merging signer responses into the original PSBT, verifying matching PSBT versions, rejecting finalized inputs, and disallowing unsafe sighash types like SIGHASH_NONE or SIGHASH_SINGLE. It also revamps the functional test mock signer to run an offline descriptor wallet that can simulate misbehaving or stripped signer responses, and enforces IWYU for the external signer module.

risk.why: A bug in PSBT merging or sighash validation could cause valid external signer transactions to be rejected or fail to sign.
